speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin our assessment, how old are you and exactly how long have you been experiencing this knee pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Given his age and the lack of trauma, is he also experiencing a limp, difficulty walking, or a high fever? I also need to know if he has had any morning stiffness or joint pain in other areas besides the knee.

DENIES FEVER, RASH, OR RECENT ILLNESSES. A DOCTOR PREVIOUSLY SUGGESTED TUBERCULOSIS BASED ON THIS PRESENTATION.

Given the patient is an 18-month-old with isolated right knee swelling, no trauma, and a strong family history of similar issues, the clinical picture strongly points towards a genetic condition rather than an infectious one like Tuberculosis, which is extremely rare in this specific presentation without systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and X-ray results are normal, which effectively rules out infection and structural bone damage like a fracture. Since this is an 18-month-old with a family history of similar issues and no trauma, I need to know if there are any visible lumps on his thigh or knee, and if he has noticed any changes in his leg length or gait pattern.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Tumor Aponeurosis (Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath)
